memory_candidates.content: When a bash script needs to hand a large JSON payload built in a shell variable to jq, prefer piping it via stdin (e.g. `echo "$big_json" | jq --argjson n "$small_scalar" ...`) or writing it to a mktemp temp file and reading it back with `--slurpfile`, rather than embedding it as a `jq --argjson name "$big_json"` command-line argument. Linux caps a single exec argv element at MAX_ARG_STRLEN (128 KiB), well below ARG_MAX (2 MB) and easy to hit with a real-scale JSON payload (a ~1 MB flattened archive failed deterministically with 'Argument list too long', exit 126). Small synthetic test fixtures rarely exceed 128 KiB, so this class of bug survives a fully green fixture suite and only surfaces against real production-scale data -- add at least one fixture case sized past the 128 KiB threshold for any jq call site that consumes a payload whose size scales with the repository's own history (an archive, an index, an accumulated log).

To live-smoke-test an orchestrator/agent-system script against a repo's own real production state.json (rather than only small synthetic fixtures) without risking any mutation to the real repo: build an isolated /tmp root, symlink its .claude/ to the real .claude/ (read-only tool access, since PROJECT_ROOT is derived from the invoking script's own path -- SCRIPT_DIR N levels up -- independent of any --state-file override), then copy (never symlink) the real specs/state.json, specs/archive/state.json, and the specific real task directories under test into the isolated root's own specs/ tree. Every write the script under test performs lands inside the isolated root; the real repo is read-only throughout. This caught a genuine jq argv-length defect (see the paired TECHNIQUE memory) that zero small fixtures had exercised.
